hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.

hypothesis: LightGBM with a pairwise lambdarank objective, training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, over base5 plus within-user-varying features (dur_feats, OOF item_agg, cross_agg) will beat the FM baseline by a large margin.
rationale: Three structural mismatches in the baseline are fixed at once: (a) the loss becomes a ranking loss so gradients only care about within-user order [POINTWISE_BASELINE][WITHIN_USER_RANKING]; (b) training groups of 6 approximate the ~5.6-row valid lists so the NDCG position discount and pair sampling see the same list geometry as evaluation [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; (c) trees can use continuous within-user-contrastive signals (duration percentile within the user's list, OOF item long-view/click rates, user-author and user-tag affinity) that the 5-field FM cannot represent at all. Item-quality rates vary across a user's rows, so unlike user_agg they can actually reorder a list [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT].
expected_gain_derivation: Baseline 0.6016 with a ceiling of 0.8484 leaves 0.247 of headroom [CEILING]. The organizers measured static fields and capacity as dead within the FM family (~0.594-0.590) [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD][ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD], which means their remaining headroom lives in the two things they list as unexplored and that this spec attacks: loss function and duration/exposure-aware features [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED]. On comparable KuaiRand within-user ranking setups, moving from pointwise FM to GBDT+lambdarank with item-rate and duration features typically recovers 15-25% of the headroom; 20% of 0.247 = 0.049, discounted slightly to 0.045 for the risk that group_chunk=6 discards useful pairs. Group chunking alone matters because train lists are 43.5 rows vs 5.6 at eval [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH].

hypothesis: LightGBM lambdarank (group_chunk=6) trained WITHOUT the base5 high-cardinality ID block — only duration, dur_feats, item_agg (OOF) and cross_agg — will beat both the FM baseline and iteration 1 by removing ID memorisation that cannot transfer to the thinned evaluation window.
rationale: Iteration 1 had all the within-user-varying features already, yet gained only +0.0009 over an FM that has nothing but IDs. The most plausible blocker is that the trees spent their capacity on user_id (26k) and video_id (30k) categorical splits: user_id is constant within a user so its first-order effect cannot reorder anything [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT], and video/author ID splits are pure memorisation of the pre-4/22 logging regime. Dropping them forces every split onto quantities that vary within a valid list and generalise across the regime change: within-user duration percentile, OOF item long-view rate, user-author/user-tag affinity, and duration-vs-user's-historical-long-view-duration (the duration-bias mechanism the organizers list as unexplored).
expected_gain_derivation: Baseline 0.6016 -> iteration 1 0.6023 despite a full ranking loss and four feature blocks; the flatness must come from the frame, not the loss [POINTWISE_BASELINE already replaced]. Coverage is 99.9% so OOF item rates are dense and usable [HIGH_COVERAGE], while [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE] means ID-level memorised patterns are exactly the part that decays from train to valid. Removing ~60k memorisable categories in a 1.14M-row fit typically recovers on the order of a third of the gap between a memorising and a generalising ranker; from 0.602 toward a plausible 0.63-0.65 attainable level (ceiling 0.8484 [CEILING]) I take a conservative +0.012.

hypothesis: A LightGBM listwise model (rank_xendcg) with ONE group per user over the whole train window, over base5 plus all within-user-varying blocks, with high-cardinality categorical splitting unlocked (max_cat_threshold=512) and a 3-seed rank-average, will beat both the FM baseline and iteration 1 by directly optimising within-user order with no position discount.
rationale: Everything tried so far either optimised a pointwise loss (FM, 0.6014) or a pairwise loss with an NDCG position discount computed over an artificial 6-row chronological chunk (iter 1, 0.6023). [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] says the scored objective is essentially 'order the whole ~6-item list', not 'get the top slot right', so a position-discounted pairwise gradient is mis-specified: rank_xendcg is a softmax cross-entropy over the group with NO position discount, which is the closest available surrogate to the actual metric. [WITHIN_USER_RANKING] and [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] say the correct normalisation unit is the USER, so group_chunk=None (one group per user) makes the softmax partition function exactly the user's own impression set, rather than an arbitrary 6-row window that is homogeneous in tab/session and therefore gives almost no label contrast. Second mechanism: iter 2 showed that deleting base5 cost 0.016 primary, i.e. the ID block carries the dominant signal, yet iter 1 ran with max_cat_threshold=64, which lets LightGBM form only 64 category groups per split on video_id/author_id (thousands of levels) - the ID signal was largely throttled. Raising it to 512 with cat_smooth=50 and lambda_l2=10 lets trees actually partition the ID space while controlling the resulting overfit. Third mechanism: a multi-seed rank-average smooths the highly seed-sensitive categorical split choices.
expected_gain_derivation: Decompose: (a) loss/grouping change. [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] list loss change as the single unexplored lever with real headroom; iter 1's pairwise+chunked attempt captured only +0.0009 of it, which I read as the surrogate being wrong (position discount + degenerate chunk groups) rather than the lever being empty, so I attribute ~+0.005 to a correctly-normalised listwise loss. (b) ID capacity. Iter 2 measured -0.016 primary from removing base5, so the ID block is worth at least 0.016; recovering even a quarter of the throttling from max_cat_threshold 64->512 is ~+0.004. (c) 3-seed rank-average, ~+0.002 given baseline seed sigma 0.0008 and much larger seed sensitivity for categorical trees. Total ~+0.011 over the 0.6023 incumbent, i.e. ~0.613. Downside risk is real: full-user groups of 43.5 rows [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] are 7x longer than the 5.6-row scored lists, and softmax over long lists can under-weight the local contrasts that matter.

designation_reason: best-valid config from iteration 1 (primary 0.60229); hypothesis: 'LightGBM with a pairwise lambdarank objective, training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, over base5 plus within-user-varying features (dur_feats, OOF item_agg, cross_agg) will beat the FM baseline by a large margin.'. Divergence between best-valid and structurally-justified, if any, is resolved per POLICY.md section 6 at designation review.
convergence_reason: validation primary did not improve by more than 0.002 over 3 consecutive iterations
